scope: Proposition 2.3 (Critical coefficient and mixed limits) of the manuscript “The critical logarithmic correction for the planar XY model” (preprints/The-critical-logarithmic-correction-for-the-planar-XY-model-October-5-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 216 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 5c357d1c416119fa), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 6-7. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. statement: For the critical parameter in (2), the Bessel height coefficient of [C] is a = a(bc) = 8π. (6) At this parameter the following fixed-geometry statements hold. (i) Let the fixed geometry belong to the polygonal Lipschitz class of [C, Theorem 3.1]: it is a finite union of bounded rectangular pieces with nondegenerate faces and widths. Pieces in one component are joined along full interfaces, which may be subdivided into 6 segments; point contacts do not join components. All passages have positive width. Allow free walls and hard pins on the primary vertices in aligned unions of positive- area boxes. On each component U, fixed bounded, piecewise continuous density smears of the height have Gaussian Laplace and moment limits with covariance the inverse of a−1 Z U |∇v|2 on {v ∈ H1 (U) : v = 0 on the pin}. For an unpinned component this is a statement about mean-free smears; its fractional mean modulo 2π becomes independent and uniform. Fixed finite-rank nonnegative penalties in box averages give the corresponding Gaussian laws, with constants integrated when the penalties confine them. The statements hold along every admissible mesh sequence, including bounded rounding of the fixed geometry. They include energy-approximable shifts in the sense of [C, Theorem 3.1]. (ii) Start with no hard pins and use the centered law whose component-local box-average penalties confine every pre-pin component constant. Let H, p be positively separated unions of boxes. Put D(H, p) = log P(hH = 0 | hp = 0) P(hH = 0) , rH(bp ) = P(hH = 0 | hp = bp) P(hH = 0 | hp = 0) . Then D(H, p) ≥ 0 converges to the Gaussian pin interaction, 0 < rH ≤ 1, and EcenrH = e−D(H,p), where the expectation samples the guard data in the centered law. For every fixed finite list of these density smears and box averages, the conditional Laplace transforms and rH admit approximations by fixed finite lists of smooth observations of the guard data, whose laws and functions converge to their Gaussian counterparts. The list is enlarged after the lattice limit. These convergence assertions also hold when the data are sampled under a fixed finite real linear tilt; D and rH retain their centered definitions above.
